# Builds Suspense for Linux, macOS, and Windows whenever something is merged
# into the release branch, and publishes a zip for each as a GitHub release.
name: Release

on:
  push:
    branches: [release]
  workflow_dispatch:

env:
  CARGO_TERM_COLOR: always

jobs:
  build:
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - name: linux-x86_64
            os: ubuntu-22.04
          - name: macos-universal
            os: macos-14
          - name: windows-x86_64
            os: windows-latest
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Install system libraries
        if: runner.os == 'Linux'
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
            pkg-config libxkbcommon-dev libxkbcommon-x11-dev libwayland-dev \
            libx11-xcb-dev libxcb1-dev libfontconfig-dev libfreetype-dev \
            libvulkan-dev

      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
        with:
          # Both Mac architectures, for one universal app.
          targets: ${{ runner.os == 'macOS' && 'aarch64-apple-darwin,x86_64-apple-darwin' || '' }}
      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
        with:
          key: ${{ matrix.name }}

      - name: Build (Linux)
        if: runner.os == 'Linux'
        run: |
          cargo build --release --locked
          mkdir -p dist/suspense
          cp target/release/suspense LICENSE.md dist/suspense/
          cd dist && zip -r ../suspense-${{ matrix.name }}.zip suspense

      - name: Build (macOS)
        if: runner.os == 'macOS'
        run: |
          cargo build --release --locked --target aarch64-apple-darwin
          cargo build --release --locked --target x86_64-apple-darwin
          version=$(sed -n 's/^version = "\(.*\)"/\1/p' Cargo.toml | head -1)
          app=dist/Suspense.app
          mkdir -p "$app/Contents/MacOS"
          lipo -create -output "$app/Contents/MacOS/suspense" \
            target/aarch64-apple-darwin/release/suspense \
            target/x86_64-apple-darwin/release/suspense
          sed "s/@VERSION@/$version/g" packaging/macos/Info.plist > "$app/Contents/Info.plist"
          cp LICENSE.md dist/
          # ditto keeps the bundle's permissions and structure intact.
          cd dist && ditto -c -k --sequesterRsrc --keepParent Suspense.app ../suspense-${{ matrix.name }}.zip
          zip -j ../suspense-${{ matrix.name }}.zip LICENSE.md

      - name: Build (Windows)
        if: runner.os == 'Windows'
        shell: pwsh
        run: |
          cargo build --release --locked
          New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force dist/suspense | Out-Null
          Copy-Item target/release/suspense.exe, LICENSE.md dist/suspense/
          Compress-Archive -Path dist/suspense -DestinationPath suspense-${{ matrix.name }}.zip

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: suspense-${{ matrix.name }}
          path: suspense-${{ matrix.name }}.zip
          if-no-files-found: error

  # Once all three have built, they're published together as one release.
  publish:
    needs: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          path: dist
          merge-multiple: true
      - name: Publish the release
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          version=$(sed -n 's/^version = "\(.*\)"/\1/p' Cargo.toml | head -1)
          tag="v${version}-build.${{ github.run_number }}"
          gh release create "$tag" dist/*.zip \
            --target "${{ github.sha }}" \
            --title "Suspense $version (build ${{ github.run_number }})" \
            --notes "Built from ${{ github.sha }} on the release branch."

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Names a release build: the version from Cargo.toml, today's date (UTC), and
# which build of the day this is, counting the releases already tagged today.
#
#   Suspense 0.1.0 (2026-09-17.2)
#
# Prints, one per line, for $GITHUB_OUTPUT:
#   version=0.1.0
#   build=2026-09-17.2                         shown in the name
#   bundle_version=20260917.2                  macOS's CFBundleVersion: numbers and dots
#   tag=v0.1.0-2026-09-17.2
#   title=Suspense 0.1.0 (2026-09-17.2)
#   file=Suspense-0.1.0-2026-09-17.2           the start of each zip's name
#
# Tags are read with `git ls-remote --tags`, from $TAGS_FROM (default origin).
# $TODAY overrides the date, for testing.
set -euo pipefail

version=$(sed -n 's/^version = "\(.*\)"/\1/p' Cargo.toml | head -1)
today=${TODAY:-$(date -u +%Y-%m-%d)}

# The highest sequence already tagged for this version today.
last=$(git ls-remote --tags "${TAGS_FROM:-origin}" "v${version}-${today}.*" \
  | sed -n "s|.*refs/tags/v${version}-${today}\.\([0-9][0-9]*\)$|\1|p" \
  | sort -n | tail -1)
sequence=$(( ${last:-0} + 1 ))

build="${today}.${sequence}"
echo "version=${version}"
echo "build=${build}"
echo "bundle_version=${today//-/}.${sequence}"
echo "tag=v${version}-${build}"
echo "title=Suspense ${version} (${build})"
echo "file=Suspense-${version}-${build}"
EOF
chmod +x .github/scripts/build-name.sh
# Test against a scratch remote with fake tags.
rm -rf /tmp/tagrepo && git init -q --bare /tmp/tagrepo && git push -q /tmp/tagrepo HEAD:refs/heads/main 2>/dev/null
echo "--- no tags"; TAGS_FROM=/tmp/tagrepo TODAY=2026-09-17 .github/scripts/build-name.sh
for t in v0.1.0-2026-09-17.1 v0.1.0-2026-09-17.2 v0.1.0-2026-09-17.10 v0.1.0-2026-09-16.5 v0.1.0-build.1 v0.2.0-2026-09-17.7; do git push -q /tmp/tagrepo HEAD:refs/tags/$t; done
echo "--- after 1, 2, 10 today"; TAGS_FROM=/tmp/tagrepo TODAY=2026-09-17 .github/scripts/build-name.sh
echo "--- next day"; TAGS_FROM=/tmp/tagrepo TODAY=2026-09-18 .github/scripts/build-name.sh | head -2

# Builds Suspense for Linux, macOS, and Windows whenever something is merged
# into the release branch, and publishes a zip for each as a GitHub release
# named for the version and the build of the day: Suspense 0.1.0 (2026-09-17.2).
name: Release

on:
  push:
    branches: [release]
  workflow_dispatch:

# One release at a time, so two on the same day can't take the same number.
concurrency:
  group: release
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  CARGO_TERM_COLOR: always

jobs:
  # Names the build once, so every platform's zip carries the same name.
  name:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      version: ${{ steps.name.outputs.version }}
      build: ${{ steps.name.outputs.build }}
      bundle_version: ${{ steps.name.outputs.bundle_version }}
      tag: ${{ steps.name.outputs.tag }}
      title: ${{ steps.name.outputs.title }}
      file: ${{ steps.name.outputs.file }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - id: name
        run: |
          .github/scripts/build-name.sh | tee -a "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

  build:
    needs: name
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - platform: linux-x86_64
            os: ubuntu-22.04
          - platform: macos-universal
            os: macos-14
          - platform: windows-x86_64
            os: windows-latest
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    env:
      # What the zip, and the folder inside it, are called.
      PACKAGE: ${{ needs.name.outputs.file }}-${{ matrix.platform }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Install system libraries
        if: runner.os == 'Linux'
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
            pkg-config libxkbcommon-dev libxkbcommon-x11-dev libwayland-dev \
            libx11-xcb-dev libxcb1-dev libfontconfig-dev libfreetype-dev \
            libvulkan-dev

      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
        with:
          # Both Mac architectures, for one universal app.
          targets: ${{ runner.os == 'macOS' && 'aarch64-apple-darwin,x86_64-apple-darwin' || '' }}
      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
        with:
          key: ${{ matrix.platform }}

      - name: Build (Linux)
        if: runner.os == 'Linux'
        run: |
          cargo build --release --locked
          mkdir -p "dist/$PACKAGE"
          cp target/release/suspense LICENSE.md "dist/$PACKAGE/"
          cd dist && zip -r "../$PACKAGE.zip" "$PACKAGE"

      - name: Build (macOS)
        if: runner.os == 'macOS'
        run: |
          cargo build --release --locked --target aarch64-apple-darwin
          cargo build --release --locked --target x86_64-apple-darwin
          app="dist/$PACKAGE/Suspense.app"
          mkdir -p "$app/Contents/MacOS"
          lipo -create -output "$app/Contents/MacOS/suspense" \
            target/aarch64-apple-darwin/release/suspense \
            target/x86_64-apple-darwin/release/suspense
          sed -e "s/@VERSION@/${{ needs.name.outputs.version }}/g" \
            -e "s/@BUNDLE_VERSION@/${{ needs.name.outputs.bundle_version }}/g" \
            packaging/macos/Info.plist > "$app/Contents/Info.plist"
          cp LICENSE.md "dist/$PACKAGE/"
          # ditto keeps the bundle's permissions and structure intact.
          cd dist && ditto -c -k --sequesterRsrc --keepParent "$PACKAGE" "../$PACKAGE.zip"

      - name: Build (Windows)
        if: runner.os == 'Windows'
        shell: pwsh
        run: |
          cargo build --release --locked
          New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force "dist/$env:PACKAGE" | Out-Null
          Copy-Item target/release/suspense.exe, LICENSE.md "dist/$env:PACKAGE/"
          Compress-Archive -Path "dist/$env:PACKAGE" -DestinationPath "$env:PACKAGE.zip"

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: ${{ env.PACKAGE }}
          path: ${{ env.PACKAGE }}.zip
          if-no-files-found: error

  # Once all three have built, they're published together as one release.
  publish:
    needs: [name, build]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          path: dist

      - name: Publish the release
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          TAG: ${{ needs.name.outputs.tag }}
          TITLE: ${{ needs.name.outputs.title }}
        run: |
          gh release create "$TAG" dist/*.zip \
            --repo "${{ github.repository }}" \
            --target "${{ github.sha }}" \
            --title "$TITLE" \
            --notes "Built from ${{ github.sha }} on the release branch."
EOF

cd /home/hyphyphyph/piton/repl && cat > .github/workflows/release.yml <<'EOF'
# Builds Suspense for Linux, macOS, and Windows whenever something is merged
# into the release branch, and publishes a zip for each as a GitHub release
# named for the version and the build of the day: Suspense 0.1.0 (2026-09-17.2).
name: Release

on:
  push:
    branches: [release]
  workflow_dispatch:

# One release at a time, so two on the same day can't take the same number.
concurrency:
  group: release
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  CARGO_TERM_COLOR: always

jobs:
  # Names the build once, so every platform's zip carries the same name.
  name:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      version: ${{ steps.name.outputs.version }}
      build: ${{ steps.name.outputs.build }}
      bundle_version: ${{ steps.name.outputs.bundle_version }}
      tag: ${{ steps.name.outputs.tag }}
      title: ${{ steps.name.outputs.title }}
      file: ${{ steps.name.outputs.file }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - id: name
        run: |
          .github/scripts/build-name.sh | tee -a "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

  build:
    needs: name
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - platform: linux-x86_64
            os: ubuntu-22.04
          - platform: macos-universal
            os: macos-14
          - platform: windows-x86_64
            os: windows-latest
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    env:
      # What the zip, and the folder inside it, are called.
      PACKAGE: ${{ needs.name.outputs.file }}-${{ matrix.platform }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Install system libraries
        if: runner.os == 'Linux'
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
            pkg-config libxkbcommon-dev libxkbcommon-x11-dev libwayland-dev \
            libx11-xcb-dev libxcb1-dev libfontconfig-dev libfreetype-dev \
            libvulkan-dev

      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
        with:
          # Both Mac architectures, for one universal app.
          targets: ${{ runner.os == 'macOS' && 'aarch64-apple-darwin,x86_64-apple-darwin' || '' }}
      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
        with:
          key: ${{ matrix.platform }}

      - name: Build (Linux)
        if: runner.os == 'Linux'
        run: |
          cargo build --release --locked
          mkdir -p "dist/$PACKAGE"
          cp target/release/suspense LICENSE.md "dist/$PACKAGE/"
          cd dist && zip -r "../$PACKAGE.zip" "$PACKAGE"

      - name: Build (macOS)
        if: runner.os == 'macOS'
        run: |
          cargo build --release --locked --target aarch64-apple-darwin
          cargo build --release --locked --target x86_64-apple-darwin
          app="dist/$PACKAGE/Suspense.app"
          mkdir -p "$app/Contents/MacOS"
          lipo -create -output "$app/Contents/MacOS/suspense" \
            target/aarch64-apple-darwin/release/suspense \
            target/x86_64-apple-darwin/release/suspense
          sed -e "s/@VERSION@/${{ needs.name.outputs.version }}/g" \
            -e "s/@BUNDLE_VERSION@/${{ needs.name.outputs.bundle_version }}/g" \
            packaging/macos/Info.plist > "$app/Contents/Info.plist"
          cp LICENSE.md "dist/$PACKAGE/"
          # ditto keeps the bundle's permissions and structure intact.
          cd dist && ditto -c -k --sequesterRsrc --keepParent "$PACKAGE" "../$PACKAGE.zip"

      - name: Build (Windows)
        if: runner.os == 'Windows'
        shell: pwsh
        run: |
          cargo build --release --locked
          New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force "dist/$env:PACKAGE" | Out-Null
          Copy-Item target/release/suspense.exe, LICENSE.md "dist/$env:PACKAGE/"
          Compress-Archive -Path "dist/$env:PACKAGE" -DestinationPath "$env:PACKAGE.zip"

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: ${{ env.PACKAGE }}
          path: ${{ env.PACKAGE }}.zip
          if-no-files-found: error

  # Once all three have built, they're published together as one release.
  publish:
    needs: [name, build]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          path: dist
          merge-multiple: true
      - name: Publish the release
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          TAG: ${{ needs.name.outputs.tag }}
          TITLE: ${{ needs.name.outputs.title }}
        run: |
          gh release create "$TAG" dist/*.zip \
            --repo "${{ github.repository }}" \
            --target "${{ github.sha }}" \
            --title "$TITLE" \
            --notes "Built from ${{ github.sha }} on the release branch."
EOF
python3 - <<'EOF'
p='packaging/macos/Info.plist'; s=open(p).read()
a="""    <key>CFBundleVersion</key>
    <string>@VERSION@</string>"""
assert a in s
s=s.replace(a,"""    <key>CFBundleVersion</key>
    <string>@BUNDLE_VERSION@</string>""")
s=s.replace("<!-- The release workflow fills in the version from Cargo.toml. -->","<!-- The release workflow fills in the version from Cargo.toml, and the build of the day. -->")
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF
python3 -c "import yaml; d=yaml.safe_load(open('.github/workflows/release.yml')); print(list(d['jobs']))"; xmllint --noout packaging/macos/Info.plist && sed -e "s/@VERSION@/0.1.0/g" -e "s/@BUNDLE_VERSION@/20260917.1/g" packaging/macos/Info.plist | grep -A1 "Version<"

content.text:
Releases will now be named like **Suspense 0.1.0 (2026-09-17.1)**. The number after the date counts that day's builds, so a second release the same day is `.2`. I haven't pushed anything, so none of this has run on GitHub yet.

**How each release is named:**

| | Example |
|---|---|
| Release title | `Suspense 0.1.0 (2026-09-17.2)` |
| Git tag | `v0.1.0-2026-09-17.2` |
| Zip files | `Suspense-0.1.0-2026-09-17.2-linux-x86_64.zip`, `…-macos-universal.zip`, `…-windows-x86_64.zip` |
| Folder inside each zip | the same name as the zip; on macOS it holds `Suspense.app` |
| macOS app version | 0.1.0, with build number `20260917.2` |

**How it works:**
- **The name:** a new script, `.github/scripts/build-name.sh`, takes the version from `Cargo.toml` and today's date in UTC. It looks at the tags already on GitHub for that version and date and uses the next number.
- **One name per release:** a first job in `release.yml` works out the name once, so all three platforms get the same name even if a build runs past midnight.
- **No clashes:** releases now run one at a time, so two merges on the same day can't get the same number.
- **The old release:** the existing `v0.1.0-build.1` release uses the old naming and is ignored when counting.

**What I checked:**
- **The numbering script:** tested against a scratch repo with fake tags:
  - With no tags it gives `.1`.
  - With `.1`, `.2` and `.10` that day it gives `.11`.
  - It ignores other dates, other versions and the old-style tag.
- **Linting:** actionlint, including shellcheck on the run scripts, reports no problems in either workflow.
- **Packaging:** the Linux packaging steps produce the expected zip layout.

The macOS and Windows steps can only run on GitHub.

**The earlier clean Linux build:** it finished. The release build compiled. 154 tests passed and 2 git pull tests failed, because that Ubuntu 22.04 image has git 2.34 and pulling needs 2.38 or newer. GitHub's runners install a newer git, but I moved the CI test job to Ubuntu 24.04 to be safe. Two follow-ups:
- **Linux release build:** it stays on 22.04, so the binary still runs on older Linux systems.
- **Pull on older git:** users on git older than 2.38 would hit the same problem when pulling in the app. That's worth a separate look.

The changes are in `.github/workflows/release.yml`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `packaging/macos/Info.plist` and the new script, all uncommitted.
